question.text: When conducting due diligence on an AIF, a key concern around the manager's competing or outside interests is that:

answer.text: Investors must be restricted from investing in other AIFs
The manager may run other funds or have outside interests that can conflict with the AIF, so alignment and the Investment Management Agreement terms need careful review
The investee company must be barred from competing in its industry
SEBI must be prevented from regulating the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.169) flags competing or outside interests of the manager as a fund-level due-diligence and alignment-of-interest concern, and pp.188-190 describe the Investment Management Agreement (IMA) as the document setting out the manager's role and responsibilities. Investors should review whether the manager runs other funds with overlapping mandates and how those potential conflicts are addressed in the IMA and the fund's conflict-of-interest framework. The Trap: The concern is about the manager's external commitments and alignment, not about restricting investors from investing in other AIFs, restricting the investee company's competition, or preventing SEBI's oversight. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.169 (competing/outside interests in fund due diligence) and pp.188-190 (IMA terms — manager role and responsibilities).
